description: The USGS Water Data APIs are the modern machine-readable route to the water data of the U.S. Geological Survey, replacing the legacy NWISWeb pages and WaterServices, which are being retired between November 2026 and February 2027. OGC API endpoints serve monitoring location metadata, time-series metadata with thresholds and units, real-time continuous measurements of streamflow, gage height and hundreds of other parameters, daily summary values for streams, lakes and wells, and field measurements; related APIs give USGS discrete water quality samples, the multi-agency Water Quality Portal, statistics on the historical record, gage camera imagery, and Real-Time Flood Impact locations where roads, bridges, embankments and buildings have been surveyed against nearby streamgages. Data are USGS public domain, free and open without registration, with a free API key for higher rate limits, and are also viewable in the Water Data for the Nation explorer and National Water Dashboard. Caveats: the platform is mid-migration so older scripts and URLs will break, provisional real-time data can be revised, and record length and parameters differ widely between sites. Simulation uses: real-time inputs for flood warning and water system digital twins, flood impact thresholds for roads and bridges, long flow and groundwater series for supply and drought planning, and calibration of hydrological and water quality models. Related records: the USACE National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams) and the NOAA National Water Model (model-noaa-national-water-model).
